record.paper_title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
record.original_question: How should Solomonoff-style induction be extended or clarified so that it can be compared to Carnap’s confirmation theory and Laplace’s rule, accommodate continuous model classes, and incorporate prior knowledge in a principled way?

evidence.quote: f) Other issues/problems. Comparison to Carnap’s confirmation theory [Car52] and Laplace rule [Lap12], allowing for continuous model classes, how to incorporate prior knowledge [Pre02, Gol06], and others.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Solomonoff's universal a priori probability is defined, for binary strings $x\in\{0,1\}^*$, by
$$M(x) \;=\; \sum_{p:\, U(p)=x*} 2^{-|p|},$$
where $U$ is a fixed universal monotone Turing machine and the sum is over all minimal programs $p$ that produce $x$ as a prefix of their output. Solomonoff induction predicts the next symbol via the conditional $M(x_{n+1}\mid x_1\dots x_n)$, and corresponds to a Bayesian mixture over the countable class of all lower semicomputable semimeasures with the universal prior $2^{-K(\nu)}$.

Develop a principled extension/clarification of Solomonoff-style universal induction that simultaneously achieves the following:

(a) Provides an explicit, formal correspondence (or precisely demarcated divergence) between universal induction and Carnap's continuum of inductive methods (the $\lambda$-confirmation functions $c_\lambda$ on a first-order monadic language) together with Laplace's rule of succession $P(x_{n+1}=1\mid x_1,\dots,x_n) = (k+1)/(n+2)$ for $k$ successes in $n$ trials; in particular, identify which choices of universal machine, prior, or hypothesis class recover $c_\lambda$ or Laplace's rule as special cases or limits.

(b) Generalizes the construction from the countable class of lower semicomputable semimeasures to genuinely continuous (uncountable) model classes $\mathcal{M}=\{\mu_\theta : \theta\in\Theta\}$ over a continuous parameter space $\Theta$ (e.g.\ a measurable subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$), specifying a computable or constructive notion of universal prior on $\Theta$, and proving convergence and loss-bound theorems analogous to Solomonoff's $\sum_{n=1}^\infty E[(M(x_n=1\mid x_{<n})-\mu(x_n=1\mid x_{<n}))^2]\le \tfrac{1}{2}\ln 2 \cdot K(\mu)$ for the true measure $\mu\in\mathcal{M}$.

(c) Provides a principled mechanism for incorporating arbitrary prior background knowledge $B$ (expressed, say, as a finite or computable set of constraints, equations, or observed data) into the universal prior, yielding a modified universal predictor $M_B$ that (i) remains dominant over the relevant class given $B$, (ii) reduces to standard $M$ when $B$ is vacuous, and (iii) admits convergence guarantees relative to $B$.

State and prove the corresponding consistency/convergence and dominance theorems for the proposed framework.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a programmatic open problem in the foundations of universal induction. There is no single agreed solution; partial work exists (e.g., Hutter and others on continuous classes via integration over parameter spaces, and Rathmanner–Hutter "A Philosophical Treatise of Universal Induction" relating Solomonoff to Carnap and Laplace), but a unified principled framework satisfying all three desiderata has not been established. Status remains effectively open.

status_evidence.title: A Philosophical Treatise of Universal Induction
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Solomonoff induction in relation to Carnap's confirmation theory and Laplace's rule, but does not provide a complete formal extension.
status_evidence.claim: Partial conceptual comparisons exist; a full principled unification remains outstanding.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
status_evidence.snippet: Lists comparison to Carnap and Laplace, continuous model classes, and incorporation of prior knowledge as open issues.
status_evidence.claim: Posed as open problems with no claimed resolution.
